skill.name: para-skill
skill.description: PARA method decision support for Obsidian and markdown knowledge bases. It classifies notes as projects, areas, resources, or archive items, then proposes safe routing, PARA frontmatter, reviews, and archiving steps.
skill.summary: Classify, route, review, and archive Obsidian notes with the PARA method.
skill.author: scifishelf

content.value_statement: Notes lose value when projects, responsibilities, and references mix together. This skill classifies Obsidian notes into PARA categories and proposes safe routing, metadata, reviews, and archiving.
actual_capabilities: Classifies notes as project, area, resource, or archive using PARA decision rules.
Suggests target vault paths based on configurable folder conventions.
Drafts PARA frontmatter while preserving unrelated metadata.
Produces hygiene reviews for inbox backlog, stale areas, project gaps, and archive candidates.
Supports defensive archiving with dry-run behavior and change logging.
Coordinates with Obsidian-oriented skills for file creation, moves, and markdown formatting.
limitations: It provides decision logic and depends on other tools for reliable file operations.
Ambiguous notes may require manual review before routing or archiving.
It does not replace Obsidian link management, dataview generation, or markdown formatting tools.
Vault paths and local conventions may need session-level configuration.

use_cases.title: Process an Inbox Backlog
use_cases.description: Classify unprocessed notes, propose target folders, and mark uncertain items for review.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Team Knowledge Vault
use_cases.description: Review project notes, recurring responsibility areas, and reference material for consistent PARA placement.

use_cases.title: Prepare Safe Archiving Decisions
use_cases.description: Identify completed or inactive notes and generate cautious archive recommendations before any move occurs.

prompt_templates.title: Classify One Note
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner classification for a single note.
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this note using PARA. Explain the type, confidence level, supporting signals, and any missing information.

prompt_templates.title: Route a Note Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate routing with no automatic changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this note and suggest the correct PARA folder. Show the current path, proposed path, confidence, and required confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize PARA Metadata
prompt_templates.scenario: Add metadata while preserving existing fields.
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest PARA frontmatter for this note. Only include fields you can justify, and do not overwrite unrelated metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Vault
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a PARA hygiene audit for this vault. Prioritize inbox backlog, project next steps, stale areas, archive candidates, and review items.

output_examples.input: A meeting note about preparing the April leadership workshop, with action items and a deadline.
output: Confidence: high, because the note has a concrete outcome, deadline, and open tasks.
Recommended path: place it under the Projects folder after user confirmation.
Frontmatter recommendation: mark it active and set a near review date.

output_examples.input: A collection of reading notes about React rendering patterns with no active tasks.
output: Confidence: high, because the content is reference material without current action pressure.
Recommended path: keep it under Resources.

output_examples.input: A project note marked done for more than 30 days, with no open tasks.
output: Confidence: medium until links and user intent are checked.
Recommended action: show a dry run and ask before moving the note.
Change log entry should be prepared if the move is approved.

best_practices: Provide the current note path, title, frontmatter, and body when asking for classification.
Keep the skill in cautious mode when reviewing a large vault or unfamiliar folder structure.
Confirm any file move, archive action, or metadata update before applying changes.
anti_patterns: Do not classify notes by topic alone without checking action relevance.
Do not archive old notes only because they have not changed recently.
Do not ask it to replace specialized Obsidian tools for links, formatting, or file moves.

faq.question: What is PARA?
faq.answer: PARA organizes information into projects, areas, resources, and archives based on action relevance.

faq.question: Does this skill move files automatically?
faq.answer: It is designed to suggest first and require confirmation for structural changes.

faq.question: Can it work outside Obsidian?
faq.answer: Yes, the decision rules can support markdown-based systems with similar folder and metadata conventions.

faq.question: Will it overwrite my existing frontmatter?
faq.answer: No. The instructions preserve non-PARA metadata and only add or update defined PARA fields.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertain notes?
faq.answer: It marks them for review, explains the uncertainty, and avoids forced classification.

faq.question: Which tools is it intended to support?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code for AI-assisted note workflows.
